crossfade.note: For a two-<audio> player: when A reaches aFrom, start B at bAt (better: at A.currentTime - (cycles - 1) * cycleSeconds) and crossfade with equal-power curves over `seconds`. Both are at the same point of the tanpura cycle with only the drone and the pad sounding; anywhere inside quietInCycle works. The pad is periodic over the whole loop, not over one cycle, so during the fade the two elements play different moments of the pad (equal-power keeps its level; its partials are not phase-aligned). The xfade file avoids this.

pad.note: An ambient drone like a shruti box: Sa, Pa and tara Sa with a soft mandra Sa, each voiced by three reeds a few cents apart (111 partials), low-passed at 600–1200 Hz (slowly breathing), with slow swells and a wide stereo image; -12.5 LU below the flute. Exactly periodic over the loop.

shimmer.note: Soft swarmandal sweeps (11 plucked strings tuned to Bhoopali, madhya to ati-tara Sa) in the breath before the phrases the score marks; never within 8 s of the loop's start or end.

xfade.note: Samples [N, N+T) repeat [0, T). Crossfade two elements inside the tail: when A reaches loopSeconds + d, start B at d; both then play identical audio.

loop.note: The whole file is one seamless loop. Decoders that read the gapless header (Chromium decodeAudioData, ffmpeg) return exactly `samples` samples: loop the whole AudioBuffer (AudioBufferSourceNode.loop = true). A decoder that ignores the header returns more, usually 1105 extra at the start (576 encoder + 529 decoder delay): then set loopStart = 1105 / sampleRate and loopEnd = loopStart + samples / sampleRate. Avoid <audio loop>: Chromium 141 skips 12–23 ms at the wrap (measured), an audible hiccup in the drone. A player that crossfades two <audio> elements should use music.tanpura.crossfade (same point of the tanpura cycle) rather than fade the end of the file into B started at 0.

sfx.note: small brass hand-bell, struck (Sa = D6, Ga ringing above; A4 = 432 Hz)
soft conch swell on Sa (D4, A4 = 432 Hz); optional
